stops.note: to fall down, to decline, from de- and cadere
carried into French for a state of moral or cultural decline, later self-indulgent luxury
stops.meaning: a state of decline, or self-indulgent luxury

stops.note: adopted from French for something excessively self-indulgent or in decline
stops.meaning: excessively self-indulgent, or in a state of moral or cultural decline

current_meaning: excessively self-indulgent, especially in luxury and pleasure
